LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the fundamental components of a computer system, understand the scope and vision of computer engineering, and appreciate the impact of technology on society and national development.
LectureTopics: Overview of computer engineering as a discipline
Computer system components: hardware, software and firmware
History and evolution of computing technology
Professional ethics and Christian values in engineering practice
AssessmentMethods: Class participation and short reflective quiz on computer engineering ethics
FeedbackComments: Excellent introduction. The ethical dimensions were well integrated. Students responded positively.

LearningOutcomes: Students will convert numbers between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal systems, apply Boolean algebra laws to simplify logic expressions, and understand how digital systems represent data.
LectureTopics: Binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal number systems
Number system conversion techniques
Boolean algebra laws and theorems
Logic gates and truth tables

Materials.Title: Number Systems and Boolean Algebra Slides

AssessmentMethods: In-class worksheet on number system conversions and Boolean simplification
FeedbackComments: Well paced. Students need additional Boolean algebra practice. Recommend supplementary exercises.

LearningOutcomes: Students will state and apply the zeroth, first and second laws of thermodynamics, analyse energy transfer in open and closed systems, and relate thermodynamic principles to real chemical engineering processes.
LectureTopics: Thermodynamic systems: open, closed and isolated
Zeroth law and temperature measurement
First law: internal energy, heat and work
Second law and entropy concepts
AssessmentMethods: Short quiz on thermodynamic system identification and first law calculations
FeedbackComments: Approved. Ensure students are comfortable with energy balance calculations before progressing to phase equilibria.

LearningOutcomes: Students will trace the historical development of management thought, compare classical and contemporary management theories, and relate ethical and servant leadership principles to management practice in Nigeria.
LectureTopics: Classical management: scientific management and administrative theory
Behavioural management theories
Contemporary approaches: systems and contingency theory
Servant leadership and Christian values in Nigerian business
AssessmentMethods: Group reflection discussion on ethical leadership qualities in contemporary Nigerian organisations
FeedbackComments: Approved. The integration of servant leadership and Christian values is commendable and aligns with university vision.

LearningOutcomes: Students will describe the functional units of a CPU, explain the fetch-decode-execute cycle, and distinguish between RISC and CISC instruction set architectures.
LectureTopics: CPU functional units: ALU, control unit and registers
Fetch-decode-execute instruction cycle
RISC vs CISC architecture comparison
Overview of ARM and x86 instruction sets
AssessmentMethods: Short written response comparing RISC and CISC architectures with examples
